rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill. It has front matter, so the `skills` site query selects it. `requirements.cli.skill_conventions` therefore applies.

The requirement says each skill's description MUST state when to use it in terms of the user's task. The front-matter `description` does this. It begins "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas", then gives concrete signals such as a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references. It also maps task types to other skills: design and any change, moves, validation findings, and adoption. It adds that the skill is the reference for directive syntax, `habeas status`, `habeas info`, and common gotchas.

The description names other bundled skills (`habeas-requirements`, `habeas-refactor`, `habeas-evidence`, `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`). The requirement allows this with MAY, so it is not a gap.

The requirement has no violation queries, so there are no matches to judge. I found no unmet obligation.
